amendments.change: Every remaining PR Title run of one pull request shares a concurrency group keyed by the pull request's number, with cancel-in-progress: true, in place of a group per review run (github.run_id). Reason: 326 queued Actions runs at 11:29Z, mostly PR Title, held required checks for hours; GitHub keeps one running and one pending run per group. The newest run repeats every check of the runs it cancels. The workflow comment saying reviews never cancel changes to match. Scratch-PR proof added: two reviews posted while a PR Title run is in progress leave at most one pending run, and the newest run's pr-title stands on the head.

The group is per event as well as per pull request: pr-title-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}, cancel-in-progress: true. Reason: with one group, a review run cancelling a running push or edit run can leave a cancelled check as the newest pr-title of pull_request events (scratch sjawhar/legion#2250 lists one pr-title per event in gh pr checks), and GitHub does not document which the ruleset reads. Per event, a run cancels only an earlier run of the same event; a pull request holds at most four PR Title runs in the queue.
